verdictReason: Killed on two majors. (1) The wedge (genre-matched creators with recent activity, no email/key chores) is already covered at $0: Steam Curator Connect (active-only list, 'No need to mess with e-mails or keys'), SullyGnome/LetsPlayIndex, and key platforms that verify active channels. (2) Freshness from public data is not exclusive; a data vendor already refreshes monthly and a free 10-streamer list is being given away. No evidence anyone pays $15-69 one-time. Pessimistic year-1 model is about -$305 before owner time. gameoutreach.co and platform ToS could not be read.

answers.question: (1) What free/cheap alternative covers the wedge?
answers.answer: Several, at $0 cash. Steam's own Curator Connect lets a developer send offers to up to 100 curators from a list limited to profiles still active in the Steam Community, with no emails or keys (D1, D2); the Steamworks page mentions no fee, and a third-party guide calls it free (not re-quoted, see unverified). SullyGnome is described as the best free tool for finding Twitch creators by game with followers/viewership (D3, D5). LetsPlayIndex shows which creators cover which game on YouTube (D4; its price and freshness were not checked). Key-request platforms are described as verifying that requestors have real, active channels (D6) and as mostly free (D7). Manual research is the DIY baseline: 'two full days minimum' (D11). A free curated list of 10 streamers per genre is being offered by an indie tool-builder in exchange for a survey (D12). Paid options exist but at different price points: a data vendor from EUR 189/month (D9) and a 'Find relevant creators' service at 350 USD/month in a 2021 article (D8). The per-launch recent-upload lookup for one game is therefore mostly a convenience bundle of free tools.

answers.question: (2) What structural edge exists and who could copy it?
answers.answer: None found. 'Data freshness' comes from public creator pages/APIs that any rival can re-pull: a generic creator-data vendor already states its database 'is refreshed monthly' (D10), free tools already expose recent coverage per game (D3, D4), and the earlier-scan claim that gameoutreach.co already sells packs from $15 (E5, unverified) means the one-time-pack position is occupied. The scan-1 edge is price (cash_cost), which is not an edge. The only plausible compounding asset is a proprietary outcome dataset (which creators answered and actually posted for paying customers), but that needs paying volume a stranger does not have on day 0 (inference). Falsifier: if paying developers who know Curator Connect, SullyGnome and LetsPlayIndex still buy a ready list at $15-69 and renew for later launches, a convenience edge would exist; nothing read shows that.

answers.question: (3) Who demonstrably pays and how much?
answers.answer: Demonstrated payers are vendors' subscription customers at much higher price points: EUR 189/month (D9) and 350 USD/month (D8, dated 2021). I found no first-hand evidence that indie developers pay $15-69 one-time for a creator list; gameoutreach.co and Keymailer prices come only from the earlier scan (E2, E5, agent_reported, not re-verified) and its blocked page could not be read. Counter-signals: the guide author says he has never paid for coverage (not quoted here) and a community manager says teams rarely budget for marketing (E7, unverified); the fraud pain is real (D13) but has a free fix (D14). A free list of 10 streamers is offered as a survey incentive (D12).

answers.question: (4) Legal / platform constraints?
answers.answer: Not settled from primary sources: the YouTube API Developer Policies and Twitch developer terms could not be fetched (permission/provenance refused), so whether a resold, API-derived creator dataset is allowed is unverified. Creator contact emails are exposed on YouTube only through the channel About tab 'Show email' action (D15), so bulk harvesting would mean automating a gated UI element, which is a ToS risk (inference). Emailing/selling creators' personal contact data raises CAN-SPAM and GDPR-type exposure (general knowledge, not verified here). Key fraud is a developer-side risk (D13); a list-only seller never handles keys, but a list containing impostor channels would be blamed for losses.

answers.question: (5) Year-1 numbers?
answers.answer: Bottom-up, every volume input is an assumption (no sourced conversion data exists). Base: $39/pack (earlier-scan model midpoint), 81 packs (2/month months 1-3, 5/month months 4-6, 10/month months 7-12) = $3,159 revenue; cost $1,362 = $550 startup (reference entrant) + $632 variable ($7.80/pack, earlier-scan model) + $180 hosting/tools ($15/month, assumption); profit about $1,797 on ~520 owner hours (about $3.5/hour). Pessimistic (price x0.8, volume x0.5, cost x1.5): revenue $1,264, cost $1,569, profit about -$305; break-even needs about 56 packs at $31.20. Does not survive pessimistic.

killReasons.reason: The wedge is already covered at $0 cash: Steam Curator Connect gives an active-only, tag-filterable curator list with no emails or keys, SullyGnome and LetsPlayIndex show who covers which game on Twitch/YouTube, and key platforms verify active channels. A $15-69 pack would only bundle free lookups.

No structural edge: data freshness is re-pullable from public data by anyone (a data vendor already advertises a monthly refresh; free tools already show recent coverage). The scan-1 edge is price, which is not an edge, and nothing exclusive or compounding is available to a stranger on day 0.

No evidence that developers pay $15-69 one-time for creator lists, while the same deliverable (a curated streamer list) is being given away free; verified paid price points are subscriptions of EUR 189-350 per month aimed at larger buyers.
Pessimistic year-1 model is negative (about -$305, break-even about 56 packs) and the base case pays about $3.5 per owner hour; volume inputs are unsourced assumptions.
Earlier-scan claim (not re-verified): gameoutreach.co already sells one-time packs from $15 after a free preview, so the one-time-pack position is occupied.

assumptions: Price $39 per pack = midpoint of the $15-69 range from the earlier-scan model (assumption, not verified).

Volume 81 packs in year 1 (2/month months 1-3, 5/month months 4-6, 10/month months 7-12): assumption for a stranger with no audience; no conversion data was found, and this input dominates the result.
Startup cash $550 per the case-file reference entrant (assumption); owner time 10 h/week about 520 h not costed.
Variable cost $7.80 per pack = 20% of $39 per the earlier-scan model (API quota, payment fees, refunds); assumption.
Base: revenue 81 x $39 = $3,159; cost 550 + 632 + 180 = $1,362; profit about $1,797.
Pessimistic (price x0.8, volume x0.5, cost x1.5): 40.5 packs x $31.20 = $1,264 revenue; cost (550+180) x1.5 + 40.5 x $11.70 = $1,569; profit about -$305; break-even about 56 packs at $31.20.
Price context: paid comparators are EUR 189/month (D9) and 350 USD/month (D8, 2021); free substitutes exist (D1, D3, D4, D12).

legalNotes: Read-only research: only public pages fetched, no logins, signups or contact. Roughly 14 distinct pages were read (19 fetch calls, some repeats to copy verbatim quotes), slightly above the ~18-read budget when counting repeats.

YouTube API Developer Policies and Twitch developer terms were NOT read (fetch refused), so API retention, resale and contact-data rules for a creator dataset are unverified; a scraping route would also need SullyGnome/LetsPlayIndex terms checked.
Creator emails sit behind the channel About tab 'Show email' action (D15); automating that is a likely ToS problem (inference, unverified).
Unsolicited commercial email to creators implies CAN-SPAM and, for EU creators, GDPR/ePrivacy exposure when selling lists of personal contact data (general knowledge, not verified in this pass).
Key fraud is a developer-side risk (D13); a list-only seller never touches keys but could be blamed if a list includes impostor channels.
unverified: gameoutreach.co page content, pack contents, creator counts and freshness (fetch refused: URL not permitted); the $15 one-time pack claim rests only on earlier-scan evidence E5.
Keymailer prices (free 10 requests/mo, $24.99/mo, boosts from $249, $149 vs $249 annual): only earlier-scan E2; keymailer.co fetch was refused.
LetsPlayIndex and SullyGnome themselves (price, freshness, export or email data): only third-party descriptions read; both sites refused.

Whether Curator Connect is free: the Steamworks page mentions no fee and a third-party guide calls it free, but that was not quoted verbatim; one read mentioned follower-count filters and a re-read said follower counts only rank/display, so do not rely on a follower filter.
YouTube/Twitch API terms, CAN-SPAM and GDPR treatment (not read).
Gamosy (KeyVault) pricing and Lurkit: Gamosy's Indie Hackers page lists no prices; Lurkit not found.
Real conversion and volume for a no-audience seller; price evidence from xsolla is from 2021.
Only 2 web searches ran before the shared search budget was exhausted, so the 'at least 3 new alternative queries' step was not fully completed.
nextStep: Drop GAM-01 unless a paying-customer signal appears that developers who already know Curator Connect, SullyGnome and LetsPlayIndex still buy a ready list at $15-69 and renew (gameoutreach.co's sales and refund data would settle it, not public pages).
